stops.name: Jerusalem, the house of David, birth of the child Jedidiah
stops.campa: In the City of David, high above the Kidron, David comforts Bathsheba his wife after the death of her first child, and she bears a son. He calls him Solomon: Shelomoh, the peaceable. But the Lord loves the boy, and by the mouth of Nathan the prophet He gives a second, hidden name: Jedidiah, beloved of the Lord. The child is raised in the palace of cedar while his father governs Israel; the prophet's word rests on him like a mantle. Peace is written into his name before he has drawn his second breath.
stops.quote: And the LORD loved him; and he sent by the hand of Nathan the prophet; and he called his name Jedidiah, because of the LORD.

stops.name: En-rogel, Adonijah's feast and the bid for the throne
stops.campa: David is old and cold, and no warmth comes into his body. Adonijah, son of Haggith, next in age after the dead Absalom, exalts himself: 'I will be king.' He gets chariots and fifty runners, and with Joab the war-chief and Abiathar the priest behind him he slays sheep and oxen by the Stone of Zoheleth at En-rogel, where the two valleys meet. He calls all the king's sons to the feast, but not Nathan, not Benaiah, not the mighty men, and not Solomon his brother. The plot is set below the city; word of it climbs the hill to the palace.
stops.quote: Then Adonijah the son of Haggith exalted himself, saying, I will be king: and he prepared him chariots and horsemen, and fifty men to run before him.

stops.name: The Gihon spring, Solomon anointed king
stops.campa: Nathan sends Bathsheba, then comes himself, and rouses the failing king. David acts: 'Take with you the servants of your lord, and cause Solomon my son to ride upon mine own mule, and bring him down to Gihon.' At the spring where the water gushes from the rock, Zadok the priest takes the horn of oil from the tent and anoints him; the trumpet sounds; and all the people cry, 'God save king Solomon!' The earth rends with the noise. Down at En-rogel Adonijah's guests hear it, tremble, and scatter. The throne is secured at the living water.
stops.quote: And Zadok the priest took an horn of oil out of the tabernacle, and anointed Solomon. And they blew the trumpet; and all the people said, God save king Solomon.

stops.name: Jerusalem, David's charge and death, the throne established
stops.campa: David's days draw near that he should die. He charges Solomon: keep the way of the Lord, walk in His statutes, that the promise stand, a man of your line upon the throne of Israel forever. Then David sleeps with his fathers and is buried in his own city. Solomon deals with those left over: Adonijah, who asks for Abishag and so asks for the kingdom, falls to Benaiah's sword; Joab is struck down clinging to the horns of the altar; Shimei is bound to Jerusalem and dies when he breaks the bound. 'And the kingdom was established in the hand of Solomon.'
stops.quote: I go the way of all the earth: be thou strong therefore, and shew thyself a man.

stops.name: Jerusalem, the marriage with Pharaoh's daughter, Gezer for a dowry
stops.campa: Solomon makes affinity with Pharaoh king of Egypt and takes his daughter to wife, and brings her into the City of David until he has finished his own house, and the house of the Lord, and the wall of Jerusalem round about. Pharaoh has gone up and taken Gezer, burnt it with fire, slain the Canaanites there, and given the city as a present unto his daughter, Solomon's wife. The kingdom of the shepherd-boy's son is grown so great that Egypt weds into it; the dowry is a walled city. Yet Solomon still sacrifices in the high places, for as yet no house is built unto the Lord.
stops.quote: And Solomon made affinity with Pharaoh king of Egypt, and took Pharaoh's daughter, and brought her into the city of David.

stops.name: Gibeon, the great high place, the dream by night
stops.campa: The Tabernacle stands still at Gibeon, the great high place, six miles northwest of the city, and there Solomon offers a thousand burnt offerings upon the altar. In the night the Lord appears to him in a dream: 'Ask what I shall give thee.' The young king does not ask for riches, nor for long life, nor for the lives of his enemies. He asks for an understanding heart to judge so great a people, to discern between good and bad. The word pleases God. He grants the understanding heart, and gives besides both riches and honour, all that was not asked. Solomon wakes; behold, it was a dream.
stops.quote: Give therefore thy servant an understanding heart to judge thy people, that I may discern between good and bad: for who is able to judge this thy so great a people?

stops.name: Jerusalem, the judgment of the two mothers and the sword
stops.campa: Two women of the streets come before the king, one living child between them, each swearing the boy is hers, the dead one the other's. There are no witnesses; the house was empty. The king calls for a sword: 'Divide the living child in two, and give half to the one, and half to the other.' Then the true mother's womb yearns for her son and she cries out: give the child to her, do not slay him. The false one says, divide it. The king knows the mother by her mercy, and gives her the child; and all Israel fears him, for the wisdom of God is in him.
stops.quote: Then said the king, Divide the living child in two, and give half to the one, and half to the other.

stops.name: Tyre, the league with Hiram, king of the Sidonians
stops.campa: Hiram king of Tyre, who ever loved David, sends his servants to Solomon. Solomon sends back word: I purpose to build a house unto the name of the Lord my God; command that they hew me cedar trees out of Lebanon. Hiram rejoices greatly and blesses the Lord who has given David a wise son over this great people. They cut a league between them, cedar and cypress for wheat and pressed oil, and there is peace between the two kings. Hiram sends also a master craftsman, another Hiram, cunning in brass, to cast the pillars and the sea.
stops.quote: Blessed be the LORD this day, which hath given unto David a wise son over this great people.

stops.name: The cedars of Lebanon, the rafts down the sea
stops.campa: Thirty thousand men are raised as a levy, ten thousand a month by courses to Lebanon; and Hiram's servants hew the great cedars on the mountain. The logs are brought down to the sea and bound into floats, and Hiram conveys them by sea to the place Solomon appoints, and there breaks them apart. The forest resins fill the air; the scent that will not rot and that insects flee is floating southward on the tide toward Joppa. Eighty thousand hewers labour in the mountains, seventy thousand bear burdens, and the timber for the house of the Lord goes down upon the waters.
stops.quote: My servants shall bring them down from Lebanon unto the sea: and I will convey them by sea in floats unto the place that thou shalt appoint me.

stops.name: The quarry beneath the mount, the stone that hears no iron
stops.campa: Great costly stones, hewed stones, are brought to lay the foundation; the stone is made ready at the quarry before it is carried up, so that neither hammer nor axe nor any tool of iron is heard in the house while it is in building. For iron is the maker of the sword, and no instrument of war may cry out over the house of peace. In the caverns under the mount, Zedekiah's Cave, the quarry of the King, the masons dress each block silent and whole, and it rises to its place without a blow.
stops.quote: And the house, when it was in building, was built of stone made ready before it was brought thither: so that there was neither hammer nor axe nor any tool of iron heard in the house, while it was in building.

stops.name: The captured demon-king: Benaiah brings Asmodeus in chains
stops.campa: How shall stone be cut without iron? The sages tell Solomon of the Shamir, the worm no bigger than a barley-corn that cleaves rock, iron and diamond at a glance, by which Moses graved the stones of the ephod. Only Asmodeus, king of demons, knows its keeping. Solomon sends Benaiah with a chain and a ring cut with the Ineffable Name. Benaiah finds the demon's pit, draws off the water and fills it with wine; Asmodeus drinks, sleeps, and wakes fettered by the Name. He is led to Jerusalem, and by his word the Shamir is fetched, and the stones are dressed in silence.
stops.quote: They said to him: There is the shamir which Moses brought to engrave the stones of the ephod.

stops.name: The Temple Mount, the ring of the Ineffable Name binds the jinn
stops.campa: The demon Ornias steals the wages and the life of a favoured boy, sucking his soul through his thumb. Solomon prays in the Temple, and the archangel Michael brings from heaven a little ring, brass and iron, graven with the Seal: the Ineffable Name of the Creator. Solomon casts it at Ornias and stamps him, then compels him to seal Beelzeboul, prince of demons, and through him all the tribes of the air. The spirits come and name themselves and their undoings, and Solomon yokes them to the work: they haul the monstrous stones, cut and lift and set, the whole host of the jinn labouring under the Name.
stops.quote: This ring; and to God, indeed, be the glory, who hath given thee this authority.
stops.quote_source: Testament of Solomon 1 (Michael's ring; trans. Conybeare)
